subject.title: [Bug]: clearUnboundScopes strips operator scopes unconditionally for non-local token-auth clients

question: Should non-local device-less shared-token/password WebSocket operator clients receive operator scopes, and should that be unconditional or gated by configured token scopes or device identity?
rationale: Current source, tests, and docs intentionally clear self-declared scopes for this class of connection, while the report shows real remote operator workflows need a trusted write-capable path; choosing that trust boundary needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Land bounded token-scope policy
options.body: Add or land a documented gateway.auth.tokenScopes-style policy with exposure guards, tests, and real Gateway proof for trusted headless/shared-token deployments.

options.title: Preserve shared-token scopes
options.body: Treat successful token/password WebSocket auth as sufficient to retain declared operator scopes and accept the broader shared-secret trust boundary.

options.title: Require device identity
options.body: Keep clearing device-less self-declared scopes and document that remote clients must use approved device identity or device tokens for write access.

recommendation.title: Land bounded token-scope policy
recommendation.body: Add or land a documented gateway.auth.tokenScopes-style policy with exposure guards, tests, and real Gateway proof for trusted headless/shared-token deployments.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete owns the open tokenScopes proposal and recent Gateway auth/config work tied to the remaining decision path.
